name: Martin Luther
role: German theologian and leader of the Protestant Reformation (1483-1546)
summary: Luther taught that God rules through two governments, a spiritual one by the Word and a temporal one by the sword, and that Christians owe rulers obedience except where commanded to sin. He attacked papal and clerical privilege, wanted rulers to restrain luxury, usury, monopolies and begging and to found schools, backed the princes against the peasants in 1525, and in later years called for suppressing Jewish worship and expelling Jews.

notes: Changed views: 1523 (Temporal Authority) heresy cannot be restrained by force and Jews should be treated kindly (That Jesus Christ Was Born a Jew); by 1543 he demanded suppression of Jewish worship, confiscation of books and expulsion, and the later position is used. On resisting the emperor he moved from absolute non-resistance (1523-25) to accepting legal armed defence of the Protestant princes (1538-39). The 1543 treatise was read in an abridged 1948 translation plus Wikipedia's summary; Admonition to Peace, Against the Peasants, Whether Soldiers Can Be Saved, On War Against the Turk and the Leisnig Ordinance were read through quotations in secondary sources, not full text. Historical rule: unspoken positions are inferred only where they follow directly from his stated views, at low confidence.
